Definition
[linear and harmonic functions]

Source: petersen:page-0298 ↗ def:pet-ch7-support-function A continuous $f:(M,g)\to \mathbb {R}$ is linear if $\Hess f\equiv 0$, i.e. both $\Hess f\ge 0$ and $\Hess f\le 0$ hold everywhere in the support sense. Then $f\circ c$ is both convex and concave along every geodesic $c$, so $(f\circ c)(t)=f(c(0))+at$; equivalently $f\circ \exp _p(x)=f(p)+g(v_p,x)$ for a fixed $v_p\in T_pM$, and $f$ is automatically $C^\infty $ with $\nabla f|_p=v_p$. More generally, $f$ is harmonic if it is continuous with $\Delta f=0$ (in the support sense).
